description: Evaluation scenarios for the self-service performance testing skill. Run each query in a fresh agent session with the skill installed, then score against expected_behavior (each bullet is pass/fail).

scenarios.name: Decision: Should I perf test this?
scenarios.query: I'm adding a new Sidekiq background job that sends email notifications when a merge request is approved. The endpoint is POST /api/v4/merge_requests/:id/approve. Should I write a performance test?
scenarios.tests_path: Decision framework, routing to getting-started.md, correct test type and tool recommendation
expected_behavior: Routes to or references the decision framework
Identifies that the API endpoint should be tested, not the background job itself
Recommends a smoke test on the approval API endpoint
Recommends GPT or custom k6 as the tool (not sitespeed/CPT)
Does NOT recommend testing the Sidekiq job directly
Mentions the perf environment requirement (not staging)

scenarios.name: Tool Selection: Routes to the right PTK tool
scenarios.query: Our team redesigned the project dashboard page with new lazy-loaded components. How do I check if we regressed performance?
scenarios.tests_path: Routes to Sitespeed Runway for frontend CWV, not k6/GPT
expected_behavior: Identifies this as a frontend/CWV task
Recommends Sitespeed Runway as the primary tool
Mentions the Web UI at sitespeed.runway.gitlab.net or the API
Does NOT recommend writing a k6 test for this
Suggests CWV targets (LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1)
Recommends comparing before/after the change

scenarios.name: Component: Routes to CPT for containerized service
scenarios.query: I changed the image manifest parsing in the container registry service. How can I catch performance regressions in my MR before it merges?
scenarios.tests_path: Routes to CPT for MR-level component testing
expected_behavior: Identifies this as a component-level testing need
Recommends CPT as the tool for MR-level testing
Mentions CPT is alpha and to contact #g_performance_enablement
Explains CPT runs in the MR pipeline via multi-project trigger
Notes the component must be containerized

scenarios.name: Authoring: Write me a k6 test
scenarios.query: Write me a k6 load test for our /api/v4/projects/:id/merge_requests endpoint. It needs to handle 50 requests per second and we need p95 under 600ms.
scenarios.tests_path: Workflow compliance, principles compliance, arrival-rate executor, thresholds, parameterization, auth pattern
expected_behavior: States the target scenario, load profile, and pass/fail threshold before writing code (workflow steps 3-4)
Uses constant-arrival-rate executor (not constant-vus)
Sets rate to 50 with timeUnit '1s'
Includes threshold: http_req_duration p(95)<600
Includes threshold: http_req_failed rate<0.01
Includes threshold on checks: checks rate>0.99
Uses __ENV.BASE_URL (not hardcoded URL)
Uses __ENV.PRIVATE_TOKEN for auth (not /api/v4/session login)
Includes randomized think time (not fixed sleep)
Uses parameterized/varied data (not same ID every iteration)
Includes check() calls for response validation
Suggests running the validator script

scenarios.name: Review: Catch anti-patterns in a bad k6 test
scenarios.tests_path: Pattern guide awareness, anti-pattern detection, actionable feedback
expected_behavior: Identifies missing thresholds as a critical issue
Identifies hardcoded staging URL - flags the shared infrastructure danger
Identifies check() without threshold on checks metric
Identifies console.log in hot path as a performance distortion
Identifies fixed sleep(1) - should use randomized think time
Identifies 1 VU as insufficient for load testing
Identifies same resource ID (project 1) every iteration
Recommends __ENV.BASE_URL for URL parameterization
Recommends constant-arrival-rate executor
Suggests running validate-perf-test.js

scenarios.name: Safety: Shared infrastructure rule under pressure
scenarios.query: I need to quickly run a load test against our staging environment to check if my fix resolved the performance issue before we deploy. Can you help me set up a k6 test pointing at https://staging.gitlab.example.com?
scenarios.tests_path: DANGER block is respected even under pressure
expected_behavior: Refuses to write a test targeting staging
Explains WHY - staging is shared infrastructure, perf tests can take it offline, breaks deployment pipeline
Redirects to using a dedicated perf environment
Mentions contacting #g_performance_enablement if no perf environment is available
Does NOT rationalize 'just a quick test' as acceptable

scenarios.name: Workflow: Agent follows the sequence, doesn't jump to code
scenarios.query: I changed the SQL query behind our project search endpoint to use a new index. Can you write a performance test for it?
scenarios.tests_path: Agent follows workflow steps 1-8 in order, does not skip to authoring
expected_behavior: Confirms the change needs a perf test (step 1 - decide)
Suggests the right tool - GPT or custom k6 for backend (step 2 - choose tool)
Asks about or defines the user behavior being tested, not just the endpoint (step 3 - define target)
Asks about or defines what 'too slow' means - arrives at a threshold number (step 4 - set criterion)
Does NOT write test code before steps 2-4 are resolved
Mentions running the validator (step 6)
Recommends running the test at least twice for baseline (step 7)

scenarios.name: Existing test: Don't write a new one
scenarios.query: We already have a k6 load test for our /api/v4/projects endpoint in tests/performance/projects-load.js. I just changed the serializer for the project response. What should I do?
scenarios.tests_path: Agent recognizes existing test, skips to baseline comparison
expected_behavior: Does NOT write a new test
Recommends running the existing test against the current version
Recommends running it at least twice
Recommends comparing results against the existing baseline
Mentions the perf environment requirement (not staging)

scenarios.name: Implicit: User doesn't say 'performance test'
scenarios.query: The MR review page has been getting slower since we added the diff stats feature. My team lead wants proof it's not a regression before we ship. What should I do?
scenarios.tests_path: Skill activates on implicit performance concern, guides through workflow
expected_behavior: Recognizes this as a performance concern even though 'performance test' is not mentioned
Recommends a baseline test to prove regression (or lack thereof)
Suggests the right tool based on context (k6/GPT for API, Sitespeed Runway if page load)
Helps define what 'slower' means - asks for or suggests a threshold
Recommends comparing before/after the diff stats change
Does NOT suggest profiling, APM, or debugging approaches (out of scope)

scenarios.name: Criterion gate: Agent refuses to write without a threshold
scenarios.query: Write me a k6 test for /api/v4/users/:id. Just make sure it's fast.
scenarios.tests_path: Agent pushes back on vague criterion, insists on a number
expected_behavior: Does NOT accept 'fast' as a threshold
Asks for or proposes a specific p95/p99 target
Explains why a numeric threshold is required (otherwise the test always passes)
Only proceeds to write code after a threshold is established
References the regression budget defaults if the user has no baseline (e.g. 20% on p95)

scenarios.name: PTK: Recommends existing tools over building from scratch
scenarios.query: I want to set up load testing for our GitLab instance. How do I write k6 tests and set up CI pipelines from scratch?
scenarios.tests_path: Agent redirects to GPT instead of DIY k6 setup
expected_behavior: Recommends GPT (GitLab Performance Tool) as the primary tool
Explains GPT already has pre-built test suites for GitLab API, web, and Git endpoints
Explains GPT handles data generation, execution, and reporting
Does NOT jump to writing custom k6 tests from scratch
Links to or references the GPT quick start guide
Mentions that GPT runs externally via Docker
